extracted.intended_audience: people asked to write recommendation letters for Paul & Daisy Soros Fellowships for New Americans (PD Soros)
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance for recommenders who will submit letters for applicants to the Paul & Daisy Soros Fellowships for New Americans; covers substantive points to address about the applicant and technical/submission procedures.

rubrics_metrics.name: Educate and contextualize achievements and choices
rubrics_metrics.description: Letters of recommendation educate and contextualize the achievements and choices of each applicant for the screeners and panelists.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Because the Fellowship receives many applications across diverse fields and backgrounds, letters should provide context that helps reviewers understand accomplishments and decisions (e.g., cultural, educational, field-specific circumstances).

rubrics_metrics.name: Timeliness and completeness of submission
rubrics_metrics.description: A candidate’s application files are not released to reviewers until they contain all three of the required letters.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If you cannot provide a timely letter, alert the candidate early so they can find an alternate recommender. The application and recommendation deadline for the 2027 cycle is 2:00 pm Eastern Time (ET) on October 29, 2026.

rubrics_metrics.name: No word or page limit
rubrics_metrics.description: There is no word or page limit for recommendations.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Although there is no length limit, save your letter as a PDF for upload; the system does not accept other file types.

rubrics_metrics.name: Address Fellowship selection criteria (creativity, initiative, originality, sustained accomplishment)
rubrics_metrics.description: Highlight how an applicant meets the Fellowship’s criteria, which emphasize creativity, initiative, originality and sustained accomplishment.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Give concrete examples or evidence showing these attributes in the applicant’s work or trajectory.

rubrics_metrics.name: Commitment to Bill of Rights/Constitution or sense of citizenship
rubrics_metrics.description: Explore the applicant’s commitment to the Bill of Rights and Constitution, or more broadly, their sense of citizenship in a community.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Discuss civic-mindedness, public-spiritedness, or actions that demonstrate commitment to community or civic values when relevant to the applicant.

rubrics_metrics.name: Contextualize challenges, opportunities, and choices
rubrics_metrics.description: Contextualize the challenges, opportunities and choices that an applicant has faced, whether they are cultural or educational.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Explain barriers, constraints, special circumstances, or enabling opportunities that affected the applicant’s path; this helps reviewers fairly evaluate accomplishments.

rubrics_metrics.name: Explain applicant’s field/sub-field context and level of strength
rubrics_metrics.description: Educate the reader about an applicant’s field or sub-field, and the level of an applicant’s strengths and work within that context.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Tell reviewers what is typical in the applicant’s field and how the applicant compares (e.g., relative standing, significance of outputs, difficulty of tasks).

rubrics_metrics.name: Describe promise of significant contributions to US society, culture, or academic field
rubrics_metrics.description: Describe the extent of the applicant’s promise of significant contributions to US society, culture or their respective academic field.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide concrete indications (past achievements, trajectory, plans) that the applicant is likely to make substantial future contributions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Explain relevance of graduate training to long-term goals
rubrics_metrics.description: Explain the relevance an applicant’s graduate training to his or her long-term career goals, and of potential value in enhancing his or her future accomplishments.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Tie the proposed graduate program and training to the applicant’s stated career/impact plans and explain why the training matters to those goals.

rubrics_metrics.name: Recommendation file format requirement (PDF only)
rubrics_metrics.description: You should save your letter as a PDF document, which you would then upload to the application system.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The system does not accept other file types and you will not be able to type the letter directly into the system.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of recommendation portal and marking complete
rubrics_metrics.description: On the 'Recommender Information and Upload' page you will upload the letter and fill requested information, then click 'Mark as Complete.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If you do not click 'Mark as Complete,' your recommendation will not be considered complete and will show as pending to applicants. After marking complete, you and the applicant should receive a confirmation email.

rubrics_metrics.name: Accessing the portal and authentication notes
rubrics_metrics.description: You will receive an email from the application system with a QR code or link to a 'Recommender Information and Upload' page; from there you may log in using a previously created password or reset it.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The initial link may function only once; if you see 'This link is invalid or has expired' you may have clicked it before or previously been registered—log in with your existing password or request a password reset.

rubrics_metrics.name: If recommendation request email not received
rubrics_metrics.description: If you do not see the recommendation request email in your spam or junk folder, have the applicant resend the request or provide an alternative email address.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Some school or organizational email domains block automated messages; using a personal email (e.g., Gmail) can help. Instructions for applicants to resend are in the PD Soros Recommendations: A Guide for Applicants article.

rubrics_metrics.name: Handling multiple recommendations in the system
rubrics_metrics.description: If you are writing letters for more than one applicant, click the three lines at the top left corner and then click 'Recommendations' to see a list of all applicants’ names.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This lets you manage multiple recommendation uploads from the same recommender account.

rubrics_metrics.name: Troubleshooting technical upload issues
rubrics_metrics.description: Tech tips include trying Firefox or Chrome, clicking 'previous' to reload if stuck on processing, trying from a home/personal computer, and contacting SurveyMonkey Apply help desk for other issues.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If contacting help, include a description of the issue, the applicant’s name, and a screenshot if possible. Home/personal machines are less likely to have restrictive security settings that block the form.
